title: fix: install archived CRAN packages from GitHub for shinyapps.io deploy job
description:
Closes #464

The "Deploy to shinyapps.io" CI job has been failing on every push to `main` because `pak` cannot resolve four packages that were archived or removed from CRAN.

**Changes:**

- `DESCRIPTION` (`Config/Needs/deploy`): replace three CRAN package names with their GitHub equivalents so `pak` can install them:
  - `biclust` → `Biclustering/biclust`
  - `metricsgraphics` → `hrbrmstr/metricsgraphics`
  - `rbokeh` → `hafen/rbokeh`
  - `maptools` removed (retired from CRAN with no maintained GitHub source)

- `examples/12_leaflet-waste/dashboard.Rmd`: remove `library(maptools)` — it was an unused import (the example uses `leaflet` and `plotly` directly, not `maptools`)

- `.github/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml`: bump `actions/checkout@v2` → `@v4` in the deploy step (was left behind from earlier updates)

title: Migrate docs from Netlify to GitHub Pages
description:
Migrate the flexdashboard pkgdown site from Netlify to GitHub Pages.

## Changes

- `_pkgdown.yml`: update `url` to `https://rstudio.github.io/flexdashboard/`
- `.github/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml`: remove `website-netlify` job (and its `NETLIFY_AUTH_TOKEN`/`NETLIFY_SITE_ID` secrets) — the existing `website` job already deploys to `gh-pages` via `pkgdown::deploy_to_branch()`
- `README.Rmd`, `README.md`: update all `pkgs.rstudio.com/flexdashboard` links

The `gh-pages` branch already contains the fully rendered site, so `rstudio.github.io/flexdashboard` is live today. A companion PR to `rstudio/pkgs.rstudio.com` will change the `pkgs.rstudio.com/flexdashboard` proxy to a 301 redirect to the new URL.

title: feat: Use "cosmo" bootswatch only if neither `preset` nor `bootswatch` are set
description:
This is a small change that will be transparent to most users that avoids errors if setting the `theme: preset` key. Currently, because bslib errors if `preset` and `bootswatch` are both set, and because `bootswatch: cosmo` is set by default by flexdashboard, users would need to write

```
output:
  html_document:
    theme:
      version: 5
      preset: shiny
      bootswatch: ~
```

to avoid the error from bslib. After this change, the `bootswatch: ~` line isn't needed.

title: Ensure flexdashboard respects knitr's collapse option
description:
Fixes #102 Previously, flexdashboard was co-opting knitr's internal `chunk` hook. We now instead first call knitr's default chunk hook before applying flexdashboard's customized chunk hook. ## Testing The document below includes two R chunks that are either collapsed or not-collapsed and two figures (to demonstrate we haven't affected the figure syntax). ### Before ![Messages collapsed](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5420529/222274279-0d0bde6f-60a6-4726-b93d-544c8dce119f.png) ### After ![Messages collapsed](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5420529/222274186-3eaec536-90a9-4e09-9547-9831945080ab.png) ### Diff Comparing the pre-rendered HTML output before and after the change (on the chunk with `collapse = TRUE`) shows that we've only affected the output. (FYI the diff is from a version with `echo = FALSE`.) ```patch
- 
[1] TRUE
- 
[1] "a"
- 
[1] "b"
+ 
[1] TRUE
+  [1] "a"
+  [1] "b"
```
knitr-collapse.Rmd ````markdown --- title: 'Messages collapsed' output: flexdashboard::flex_dashboard: orientation: row --- ## Row ### Collapsed ```{r echo = TRUE, collapse = TRUE, message = TRUE, comment = "#>"} knitr::opts_current$get("collapse") print("a") print("b") ``` ### Not collapsed ```{r echo = TRUE} print("c") print("d") ``` ## Row ### A wide plot ```{r, fig.width=10, fig.height=5} hist(faithful$waiting) ``` ### A tall plot ```{r, fig.width=5, fig.height=10} hist(faithful$waiting) ``` ````

title: Support icons for navigation menus
description:
Supports an additional data attribute syntax to provide icons for navigation dropdown menus.

Previously, we supported icons only on page menu items, which are provided with the `data-icon` attribute. Multiple pages can be included in a single navigation menu by providing all collected pages with the same `data-navmenu` attribute value. 

For example, these two pages are included in a nav menu title "Topics".

````markdown
---
title: Issue 383
output:
  flexdashboard::flex_dashboard:
    orientation: columns
    vertical_layout: fill
---

# Pie Charts {data-icon="fa-chart-pie" data-navmenu="Topics"}

Pie Charts is accessed via a submenu entitled 'Topics'

# Info {data-icon="fa-info" data-navmenu="Topics"}

Info is also accessed via a submenu entitled 'Topics'
````

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5420529/221015823-7ffae0ae-fcc1-454f-b35e-939a4cacf246.png)

This change allows users to provide an icon for the navigation menu by providing the icon name in the `data-navmenu-icon` attribute. The first usage of navmenu must have this attribute for it to be added correctly.


````markdown
---
title: Issue 383
output:
  flexdashboard::flex_dashboard:
    orientation: columns
    vertical_layout: fill
---

# Pie Charts {data-icon="fa-chart-pie" data-navmenu="Topics" data-navmenu-icon="fa-map-signs"}

Pie Charts is accessed via a submenu entitled 'Topics'

# Info {data-icon="fa-info" data-navmenu="Topics"}

Info is also accessed via a submenu entitled 'Topics'
````

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5420529/221015847-14e40912-cf48-4443-ade7-fc6d76b8d897.png)


Closes #383

title: Fix active nav menu markup
description:
Fixes #411 This is a minimal fix for the behavior described in #411. The root issue is that BS5 requires a `.tab-pane.active` to have a corresponding `.active` toggle item. I'm being vague because the active class can appear as either `li.nav-item.active` or `.nav-link.active`. When the active class is imbalanced in the markup in BS5, the `.active` class isn't removed from the imbalanced `.tab-pane` until after it's activated. https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5420529/220937196-748eb254-4f90-44f0-93b3-46c2736bf4d8.mp4 The clip above uses the markup created by flexdashboard during initialization just [before the Bootstrap tab plugin is invoked](https://github.com/rstudio/flexdashboard/blob/bf8cdc55e15e3a7cfc53ed2d186a9303d271dc48/inst/www/flex_dashboard/flexdashboard.js#L135-L136). You can observe the tab behavior in Bootstrap versions 3-5 using this Rmd:
bootstrap-tabs-init.Rmd ````markdown --- title: BS Nav Test output: html_document: theme: version: 5 self_contained: false --- > Bootstrap version x.y.z ⏱️ before initializing tabs ## No active classes anywhere ```{=html}
  • One
  • Two
  • Three
one content
two content
three content
``` ## Nav doesn't have active class ```{=html}
  • One
  • Two
  • Three
one content
two content
three content
``` ## Nav has active class on li ```{=html}
  • One
  • Two
  • Three
one content
two content
three content
``` ## Nav has active class on li > a ```{=html}
  • One
  • Two
  • Three
one content
two content
three content
``` ```{=html} ``` ```{js echo=FALSE} $(function() { const bs_v = $.fn.tab.Constructor.VERSION; console.log(`Bootstrap version: ${bs_v}`); document.getElementById('bs-version').innerText = bs_v; }) $('#activate').on('click', function() { ['no-active', 'nav-no-class', 'nav-class-li', 'nav-class-li-a'] .forEach(id => { console.log( `activating #${id}, active elements:`, document.querySelectorAll(`#${id} .active`) ) $(`[href="#${id}-two"]`).tab('show') }) $('#state').text('✅ tabs ready') }) ``` ````
Testing across all the three major versions of Bootstrap reveals that adding the `.active` class to the nav list item maintains consistent appearance and behavior across all versions, even if the tab plugin were to fail for some reason. | BS | Before | After | |:--:|:--:|:--:| | 3 | ![bs3-before](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5420529/220939006-03eaec58-6f7f-41c7-b25c-f33eaa0bac0b.png) | ![bs3-after](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5420529/220939030-65be7bfa-07f9-4fdd-a066-fe0e07087674.png) | | 4 | ![bs4-before](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5420529/220939085-a566e437-8822-494b-889e-c1cfba587698.png) | ![bs4-after](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5420529/220939101-9d0d3519-5733-422b-93c1-8a6f9dd22470.png) | | 5 | ![bs5-before](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5420529/220939179-adfe3590-a580-489d-a321-b1616ca5bdc7.png) | ![bs5-after](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5420529/220939194-4334a9e2-72c8-40be-a4f8-f89ae4492da4.png) |

title: When using bslib, default to bootswatch: cosmo
description:
`flex_dashboard`'s `theme` default value is effectively [cosmo](https://bootswatch.com/3/cosmo/). Currently, when opt-ing into bslib usage, you don't get cosmo (you just get Bootstrap defaults), which can be surprising since to get different accent colors, etc. 

With this change, if you don't specify `bootswatch`, then you'll now get cosmo. For example, this yaml: 

````
---
output: 
  flex_dashboard:
    theme:
      version: 4
---
````

Is equivalent to:

````
---
output: 
  flex_dashboard:
    theme:
      version: 4
      bootswatch: cosmo
---
````

You can still use a different Bootswatch themes, and once https://github.com/rstudio/bslib/pull/308 lands, you'll be able to opt-out of Bootswatch entirely with

````
---
output: 
  flex_dashboard:
    theme:
      version: 4
      bootswatch: default
---
````

title: Allow valueBox() and gaugeSector() to be dynamically themed
description:

````
---
title: "Tabset Row"
runtime: shiny
output: 
  flexdashboard::flex_dashboard:
    theme: 
      version: 4
---


```{r, include=FALSE}
library(flexdashboard)
bslib::bs_themer()
```

## Value Boxes {data-width=200}

### Primary

```{r}
valueBox(1, caption = "Reflects primary color", icon = "fa-github")
```

### FA info

```{r}
valueBox(2, caption = "Reflects info color", color = "info", icon = "ion-social-twitter")
```

### FA success

```{r}
valueBox(3, caption = "Reflects success color", color = "success", icon = "glyphicon-time")
```

### FA warning {.bg-primary}

```{r}
valueBox(4, caption = "Reflects warning color", color = "warning", icon = "fa-facebook")
```

### FA danger

```{r}
valueBox(5, caption = "Reflects danger color", color = "danger", icon = "fa-facebook")
```

### FA custom

```{r}
valueBox(
  6, caption = "custom", color = "lightgray", 
  icon = "fab fa-r-project"
)
```

## Gauges {data-width=200}

### Reflects success color

```{r}
gauge(91, min = 0, max = 100, symbol = '%', gaugeSectors(success = c(80, 100)))
```

### Reflects warning color

```{r}
gauge(37.4, min = 0, max = 50, gaugeSectors(warning = c(21, 40)))
```

### Reflects danger color

```{r}
gauge(7, min = 0, max = 10, gaugeSectors(danger = c(7, 10)))
```

````

title: CanvasXpress FlexDashboard Example
description: We would like to submit a canvasXpress example for your flexdashboard examples site that showcases the use of CanvasXpress to visualize genetic data.  The R canvasXpress package enables use of the CanvasXpress JavaScript library as an HTMLWidget.  Visualizations created with this package support up to millions of drawing objects in a performant manner, as CanvasXpress was developed as the core visualization component for bioinformatics at Bristol-Meyers Squibb.  More details about this unique visualization library as well as hundreds of visualization examples and full API documentation can be found at http://canvasxpress.org.

title: fix unicode in navbar, closes #125
description:
This ought to fix #125, i.e. that navbar links do not show up or stop pandoc when they contain unicode characters. The problem is that `writeLines` in `as_tmpfile` writes the `str_tmpfile` in the native encoding, but pandoc expects it to be "UTF-8". (`as_tmpfile` is (only) called by `pandoc_navbar_args`).

Following @kevinushey's [lead](https://kevinushey.github.io/blog/2018/02/21/string-encoding-and-r/) here to ensure that `as_tmpfile` writes really writes in UTF-8 encoding.

title: Use the html4 output format instead of the default html5 in Pandoc 2.0
description:
Fixes #149.

Basically Pandoc 2.0 starts to default to `html5` when the output format is the ambiguous `html` (previously it was `html4`), and the consequence is that the section divs actually use the `<section>` tag instead of `<div>`. See https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/pandoc-discuss/d-d07z2iHJs for more information.

I have compared the output with this PR + Pandoc 2.0 against Pandoc 1.19, and the output files seem to be identical.
